title: Ionic conductivity
hints: Compare ion mobility between solid and liquid.
Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
solution: In the melt, $\ce{Mg^2+}$ and $\ce{Cl^-}$ can move and carry charge.
statement:
Why does molten magnesium chloride conduct electricity much better than its solid?

[_]{a}

choices: Its ions are mobile in the melt.
It produces free metallic electrons on melting.
explanations: Ionic conduction is carried by ions.
Neutralizing the carriers would not explain conduction.
Melting does not undo the ionic charges.
